provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the Tours Mame 1922 reads 'Ge' where the 1962 prints 'Sanctorum'; the Tours Mame 1922 window carries ':' at this point where the 1962 does not; the Tours Mame 1922 sets no pointing after 'praesidia' where the 1962 sets a colon; recogniser damage in the Tours Mame 1922 text layer at this locus, not variant readings: tuérum for tuorum; Susanne for susanae; presidia for praesidia; bare numeric tokens (printed folio / marginal numbers) dropped from the Tours Mame 1922 reading: 3° 13‘, 20 510; conclusion length was not collated: the 1962 prints 'Per Dominum nostrum.' and the witness abbreviates the same rubrical cue; one formula at two lengths, which is within the matched tolerance. Corroboration: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, nearest preceding printed-folio marker 516 at text-layer line 71280; text-layer lines 71350-71370 (char-level agreement 0.934 with the 1962 target).

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Sanctorum Martyrum tuorum Tiburtii et Susannae nos, Domine, foveant
continuata praesidia: quia non desinis propitius intueri; quos talibus
auxiliis concesseris adjuvari. Per Dominum nostrum.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Adesto, Domine, precibus populi tui, adesto muneribus: ut, quae sacris sunt
oblata mysteriis, tuorum tibi placeant intercessione Sanctorum. Per Dominum
nostrum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Sumpsimus, Domine, pignus redemptionis aeternae: quod sit nobis, quaesumus,
intervenientibus sanctis Martyribus tuis, vitae praesentis auxilium pariter
et futurae. Per Dominum.
